requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement IS a statement that expresses sets of possible alternatives forming a tree of possible execution paths.
requirements.original: An alt statement expresses sets of possible alternatives that form a tree of possible execution paths.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement has the syntax `alt` [`@nodefault`] "{" followed by optional local variable, timer, constant or template definitions, followed by alternatives of the form "[" [BooleanExpression] "]" with either a timeout, receive, trigger, getcall, catch, check, getreply, done or killed statement followed by a statement block, or an altstep instance followed by an optional statement block, and an optional final "[" `else` "]" StatementBlock, closed by "}".
requirements.original:
alt [ @nodefault ] "{" 
       { ( VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) [";"] }
       { 
        "[" [ BooleanExpression ] "]" 
            ( ( TimeoutStatement |
               ReceiveStatement |
               TriggerStatement |
               GetCallStatement |
               CatchStatement |
               CheckStatement |
               GetReplyStatement |
               DoneStatement |
               KilledStatement ) StatementBlock ) 
             | 
            ( AltstepInstance [ StatementBlock ] )
       } 
       [ "[" else "]" StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement denotes branching of test behaviour due to the reception and handling of communication events, timer events and/or the termination of parallel test components, using the operations `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `check`, `timeout`, `done` and `killed`.
requirements.original: The alt statement denotes branching of test behaviour due to the reception and handling of communication and/or timer events and/or the termination of parallel test components, i.e. it is related to the use of the TTCN-3 operations receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, catch, check, timeout, done and killed.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement denotes a set of possible events that are matched against a particular snapshot.
requirements.original: The alt statement denotes a set of possible events that are to be matched against a particular snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement MAY define local definitions before its alternative branches.
requirements.original: An alt statement may define some local definitions before its alternative branches.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition of an `alt` statement CAN be used by all branches of that `alt` statement.
requirements.original: These can be used by all the branches.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement is entered, a snapshot IS taken.
requirements.original: When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains local definitions
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains local definitions before its first branch, the local definitions ARE evaluated before the snapshot is taken.
requirements.original: If the alt statement contains local definitions before its first branch, these are evaluated before the snapshot is taken.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a repeat statement is executed in the alt statement
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement executes the `repeat` operation, the whole `alt` statement, including its local definitions, IS re-evaluated.
requirements.original: When the alt statements executes the repeat operation, the whole alt statement, including the local definitions, is re-evaluated.

ambiguity.issue: "repeat operation" is used, while clause 20.3 names it the repeat statement; also "alt statements executes" is grammatically garbled.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The alternative branches of an `alt` statement, the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and the top alternatives of altsteps activated as defaults ARE processed in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: The alternative branches in the alt statement and the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and altsteps that are activated as defaults are processed in the order of their appearance.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: If several defaults are active, the top alternatives of the defaults ARE evaluated in the reverse order of the activation of the defaults.
requirements.original: If several defaults are active, the reverse order of their activation determines the evaluation order of the top alternatives in the defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The alternative branches in active defaults ARE reached by the default mechanism.
requirements.original: The alternative branches in active defaults are reached by the default mechanism described in clause 20.5.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives ARE ignored for the execution of that `alt` statement.
requirements.original: If the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: An alternative branch IS either a branch that may be guarded by a Boolean expression or an else-branch, i.e. a branch starting with `[else]`.
requirements.original: The individual alternative branches are either branches that may be guarded by a Boolean expression or else-branches, i.e. alternative branches starting with [else].

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An else-branch IS always chosen and executed when it is reached.
requirements.original: Else-branches are always chosen and executed when they are reached (see below).

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: A branch that may be guarded by a Boolean expression IS either an altstep-branch (invoking an altstep), a done-branch (starting with a `done` operation), a killed-branch (starting with a `killed` operation), a timeout-branch (starting with a `timeout` operation) or a receiving-branch (starting with a `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` or `check` operation).
requirements.original: Branches that may be guarded by boolean expressions either invoke an altstep (altstep-branch), or start with a done operation (done-branch), a killed operation (killed-branch), timeout operation (timeout-branch) or a receiving operation (receiving-branch), i.e. receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, `catch or a check operation.

ambiguity.issue: Editorial: misplaced backticks span across this sentence and the next one in the source.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean guard SHALL be based on the snapshot.
requirements.original: The` evaluation of the Boolean guards shall be based on the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard IS considered fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined or if the Boolean guard evaluates to `true`.
requirements.original: The Boolean guard is considered to be fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined, or if the Boolean guard evaluates to true.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled.
requirements.original: An altstep-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.
requirements.original: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, i.e. the altstep is invoked and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch MAY contain an optional statement block.
requirements.original: An altstep-branch may contain an optional statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: The optional statement block of an altstep-branch SHALL be executed only if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.
requirements.original: The optional statement block shall be executed only, if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:done-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the stopped list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A done-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A done-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:done-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a done-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `done` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the done operation.

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: A `done` operation in a selected done-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.original: The done operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the killed list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A killed-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A killed-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a killed-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `killed` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the killed operation.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-operation
requirements.canonical: A `killed` operation in a selected killed-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.original: The killed operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A timeout-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A timeout-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a timeout-branch causes the execution of the specified `timeout` operation, i.e. the removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the `timeout` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the specified timeout operation, i.e. removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the timeout operation.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria are fulfilled
requirements.canonical: A receiving-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria of the receiving operation are fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.
requirements.original: A receiving-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the matching criteria of receiving operation is fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a receiving-branch causes the execution of the receiving operation, i.e. the removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, possibly an assignment of the received information to a variable, and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the receiving operation, i.e. removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, maybe an assignment of the received information to a variable and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria of the trigger operation are not
requirements.canonical: In a receiving-branch with a `trigger` operation, the top message of the port queue IS removed also if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria are not.
requirements.original: In the case of the trigger operation the top message of the queue is also removed if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria is not.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria of the trigger operation are not
requirements.canonical: If the Boolean guard of a `trigger` branch is fulfilled but its matching criteria are not, the statement block of that alternative IS NOT executed.
requirements.original: In this case the statement block of the given alternative is not executed.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a snapshot IS described as a series of indivisible actions of a test component.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The TTCN-3 semantics describe the evaluation of a snapshot as a series of indivisible actions of a test component.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 semantics DO NOT assume that the evaluation of a snapshot has no duration.
requirements.original: The semantics do not assume that the evaluation of a snapshot has no duration.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: Events occurring during the evaluation of a snapshot (component stops, timer timeouts, new messages, calls, replies or exceptions entering port queues) DO NOT change the actual snapshot and ARE NOT considered for its evaluation.
requirements.original: During the evaluation of a snapshot, test components may stop, timers may timeout and new messages, calls, replies or exceptions may enter the port queues of the component However, these events do not change the actual snapshot and thus, are not considered for the snapshot evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.canonical: Due to dynamic test configurations, a receiving-branch CAN refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Due to the possibility of defining dynamic test configurations, a receiving branch may refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port belongs to the receiving component, and matching IS related to the top elements in the port queues.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A dynamically unmapped or disconnected port contributes to a snapshot in the same manner as a mapped or connected port.
requirements.original: Dynamically unmapped and disconnected ports contribute to a snapshot in the same manner as mapped and connected ports.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: The execution of receiving operations MAY empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.
requirements.original: This means, the execution of receiving operations may empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: no alternative can be selected and executed
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternative branches in an `alt` statement and none of the top alternatives in the invoked altsteps and active defaults can be selected and executed, the `alt` statement SHALL be executed again, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the evaluation of the alternative branches is repeated with the new snapshot.
requirements.original: If none of the alternative branches in the alt statement and top alternatives in the invoked altsteps and active defaults can be selected and executed, the alt statement shall be executed again, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the evaluation of the alternative branches is repeated with the new snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: The repeated evaluation of an `alt` statement SHALL continue until an alternative branch is selected and executed, the test case is stopped by another component or by the test system, or a dynamic error occurs.
requirements.original: This repetitive procedure shall continue until either an alternative branch is selected and executed, or the test case is stopped by another component or by the test system (e.g. because the MTC is stopped) or with a dynamic error.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: a test component is completely blocked
requirements.canonical: If a test component is completely blocked, the test case SHALL stop and indicate a dynamic error.
requirements.original: The test case shall stop and indicate a dynamic error if a test component is completely blocked.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component IS completely blocked when none of the alternatives can be chosen, no relevant test component is running, no relevant timer is running and all relevant ports contain at least one message, call, reply or exception that does not match.
requirements.original: This means none of the alternatives can be chosen, no relevant test component is running, no relevant timer is running and all relevant ports contain at least one message, call, reply or exception that do not match.

readings: A test component IS completely blocked when no alternative can be chosen and no test component, timer or port referenced in the alternatives of the alt statement (including invoked altsteps and active defaults) could change the situation.
A test component IS completely blocked when no alternative can be chosen and no test component or timer of the whole test configuration that is relevant to any future event is running.
ambiguity.issue: The term "relevant" for components, timers and ports is not defined; the first reading (relevant = referenced in the alternatives being evaluated) is chosen as most likely.
